title: THE STANDING BOARD — VOSK'S CHAMBERS, UNSEALED
revisit: The chambers. Four case-files open on the cogitator, a ledger you may or may not be keeping, and four places in this hive that a dead man was looking at.
intro:
Eight days.

The Crown reclaimed the chambers at the close of the case and crated the
effects, and then somebody in the Provost's office worked out that the
investigating officer of a closed matter has no standing to be given a room
and the officer of an *open* one does, and so the case was reopened, on a
form, by you, and the room came back.

It is the same room and it is not. The furniture has been packed and
unpacked by people who did not know the arrangement mattered.

The cogitator boots the way it has booted every morning for three years, and
four of Hadrian Vosk's case-files come up open.

  FENN/CUSTODY
  SUMP-VARIANCE
  ECCL/ALMS
  GALLERY-9

He never left a file open. He closed them the way other men lock doors, at
the end of a shift, finished or not, because an open file is a thing somebody
else can read.

These have been open eleven weeks. Long enough that the cogitator has stopped
asking whether you want to save them.

He was pointing, for eleven weeks, and nobody in this hive was looking at his
desk.
look:
His chambers, reopened on a form, with your name on the form.

The COGITATOR, and four dormant CASE-FILES open on it: Fenn's custody, a sump
variance, an Ecclesiarchy alms account, and Gallery 9.
The DESK, repacked and unpacked by strangers.
Your LEDGER, if you are keeping one, and your notebook, which you are.

Sergeant Oduya on the landing. Savant Fenn wherever you have put him.
Vesse Talm on the threshold, and not across it.

objects.careless: Four case-files, open, dormant, eleven weeks old. FENN/CUSTODY. SUMP-VARIANCE. ECCL/ALMS. GALLERY-9.
objects.careful:
None of them is a case. That is the first thing.

A case-file has a complainant, an assessment and a disposition. These have a *name* and a *query string* and nothing else — they are the shape a file makes when somebody opens it to have somewhere to put a thought, and then does not put the thought in it.

FENN/CUSTODY is his own savant. SUMP-VARIANCE is eleven crowns in a district assessment. ECCL/ALMS is a Cathedral disbursement account. GALLERY-9 is a manufactorum.

Four things that have nothing to do with each other, in a hive of nine million things, held open for eleven weeks by a man who closed files the way other men lock doors.

objects.careless: Cael-pattern, three years old, beautifully maintained. His authority key opens it and the key is yours.
objects.careful:
It has two places to put a thing, and it has always had two, and until this week you had only ever used one.

The CASE-FILE is indexed, searchable, cross-referenced, requisition-eligible and readable by anything with standing to read it. Everything you have ever filed is in there and everything in there is a thing somebody can act on.

The other is a blank field labelled LEDGER, which does nothing at all: no index, no search, no cross-reference, no requisition. It is a place to write by hand and it is functionally a drawer.

Hadrian Vosk kept eleven years of casework in longhand in a room with this machine in it, and you have spent eight days deciding that was vanity.

objects.careless: The desk, the side table, the shutter, the chair. All of it back. None of it where it was.
objects.careful:
The board is on the side table because somebody put it back on the side table, and the pieces are in the box because somebody put them in the box, and the shutter is closed because a warden closed it.

Whatever was arranged in this room was arranged eight days ago and unarranged four days ago by two Crown porters with a manifest, working carefully, in good faith, at speed.

It is the second time this week you have watched something true be destroyed by people doing their jobs correctly.

npcs.title: Vesse Ilaria Talm
npcs.topic_refusal: "From out here," Ilaria says. "I'll answer anything from out here."
npcs.portrait: Vesse Ilaria Talm, on the landing side of the threshold, one hand flat on the frame, not coming in.
npcs.greeting:
She stops at the threshold and does not cross it.

"I'll wait here, sir, if that's all the same."

"It's a room, Vesse."

"It isn't." She has her hand flat on the door frame and her head slightly turned. "Rooms have a shadow. Every room in this hive has a little wash off the vox-plate and the relay, and you don't hear it, and I do, and I have for twenty years the way you don't hear your own blood.

"This one has none. It's not quiet, sir. It's *absent*. He took the plate out."

She is not being poetic. She is describing an instrument reading.

"I'd rather stand on the landing. I can hear you perfectly well from the landing."
npcs.reprise: She waits on the landing with a hand on the frame.
npcs.unknown: "I don't know," Ilaria says, from the landing.

topics.text:
"Forty hours of raw cylinder," she says. "Inside the Choir, on the Spire, with the relay live, because the reproducer is bolted to a bench eleven flights down and it is not coming up here for me.

"Unshielded. There's no shroud for it and there's no shift pattern for it and there is no version of it where I do six hours and stop, because the rote only comes up out of the noise when you've had enough of the noise to stop hearing it."

She is very calm and she has clearly worked all of this out before she opened her mouth.

"After it I'll be able to carry grain and tithe. I'll not be able to carry anything that matters, ever again, and the Choir-Prefect will put that on a form as *reduced sensitivity following extended exposure*, which is a true sentence.

"I'd like you to have me say it plainly, so that neither of us can be vague about it later. It ends the part of me you have any use for."

"Forty-one seconds," Ilaria says. "I've been afraid of forty-one seconds for eleven weeks. Forty hours is the same thing eight hundred times. That's arithmetic."

It is not arithmetic and you both know it.

Her own cylinder is in that vault. It is in the 0997 drawer, second quarter, filed by year and by nothing else, and to find the rote in nineteen years of a dead man's dictation she will have to go past it — not once, and not carefully.

"You'll want to be somewhere else," she says. "Not out of kindness. If you're in the room I'll perform, and performing takes longer."

She puts her hand back on the frame.

"Send me down, sir. I'd rather be sent than volunteer. It's the last bit of it that's mine."

"No, sir."

She does not soften it and she does not take any time over it, which tells you she has already been round it.

"There's the wax and there's the traffic. The wax is me. The traffic is your savant, and I'd rather you asked me than him, and I'd rather say that out loud than have you think I was being noble about it.

"There's no third one. There's no clever one. You've been looking for a clever one for about four minutes and I've been watching you do it."

"Every room has one," Ilaria says. "The plate hums, the relay bleeds, there's a — I've never had to describe it. It's a floor. You stand on it.

"He took the plate out of this room. Not disabled — *out*, and the socket capped. I've asked the warden and it's on the maintenance ledger, four years ago, at his own request, at his own cost, because the Crown wouldn't pay to remove a working instrument."

"Four years ago."

"Four years and two months." A pause. "There isn't another room in the Adamant Crown like it, sir. I've been in most of them. He made one place in this building that nothing can hear, and then he sat in it for four years, and then he arranged his own furniture and died in it."

[ B0 corroborated — he built the room before he used it ]

"I'm on light carriage, sir. The Choir-Prefect's put me on grain and tithe until there's a finding." She says it evenly. "I'd rather be working."

"You are working."

"I'm standing on a landing." Something that is almost a smile. "You've had me up here four times in eight days to be an instrument, sir, and I'm not complaining, I'd rather be an instrument than a suspect. But I would like to know which one I am on the form, when there's a form."

"I've thought about very little else," Ilaria says.

"And?"

"And I've decided I don't want to hear it again, which I'd like on the record as my own decision and not something anybody spared me." Her hand is still flat on the frame. "It's my voice. It's my mouth. Whatever came through me came through me in the ordinary way, at the ordinary time, on an ordinary channel, and I countersigned a summary of it afterwards that was wrong.

"That's not a psyker going bad, sir. A psyker going bad is loud. This was *tidy*."

beats.text:
"Can I ask you something, sir, and you can tell me it's not my business."

She is still on the landing.

"When they cleared this room — did you get what you wanted out of it first? Only they were quick. Provost's men were in here on the ninth morning with crates and a stencil, and it took them a day and a half, and I stood on this landing and watched them do it."

"Where did it go?"

"Vault. Effects holding, wherever they put that. It's all still somewhere, sir; they don't throw an Inquisitor's things away, they just stop being able to find them."

She says it as small talk, because it is small talk, and goes back to waiting on the landing.

"You've got half of it," Ilaria says, from the landing. "The room half. And the man who had the other half is dead."

It is not a question and you do not answer it.

"He never wrote it down, sir. That's the thing nobody's said out loud yet. A key that's written down is a key somebody can take, so he didn't write it down — he *used* it. Nineteen years of dictation in it, out of his own mouth, to a Choir."

Her hand comes off the door frame for the first time since you have known her.

"Every dispatch out of this building goes through the Spire and every dispatch through the Spire gets cut into wax, because a rescript from 604 says it must. Nineteen years of a man speaking a cipher out loud, in the same rote, in the same mouth-shapes, over and over, and all of it is sitting in a drawer eleven flights under the cells with no index on it below the year.

"It isn't written down anywhere. It's *said* down. And I'm the only person you have who can hear it."

shows.text:
You read it to them. All of it, out of the notebook, standing up, in the room
it was written in.

Ilaria does not move from the landing and does not interrupt, and when you
have finished she says, "Nine hundred million," and then nothing for a while.

"He knew. All the years I was carrying for him, he knew that."

"He signed it."

"Yes, sir. And then he spent eighty-one years being the man who signed it,
which is a longer sentence than they'd have given him."

Sergeant Oduya has been in the doorway for the last third of it with a mug
going cold in her hand.

"What's a tithe dispute," she says.

It is not a question about vocabulary. You start to answer it twice and stop
both times, and in the end you tell her the truth, which is that it is an
argument about a number between two offices, and that it went the way
arguments about numbers go, and that four hundred million of the nine were
children.

Bez puts the mug down on the crate very carefully, the way you put a thing
down when your hands have stopped being reliable.

"Right," she says. "Tell me what we're doing, sir, and I'll go and get my
coat."

[ ILARIA_TRUST +1 ]

acts.text:
You ask her.

"Thank you," Ilaria says, which is not what you were braced for, and goes down the eleven flights on her own without waiting to be escorted.

It takes six days. She works in four-hour blocks because the Prefect's warden will not sign anything longer, and then in six-hour blocks because the warden stops coming, and by the fourth day she has stopped going up to the cells to sleep and is sleeping on a drawer-step in her coat.

You are not in the room. She asked you not to be, and you find on the third day that you had been going to be anyway, and that the reason was not kindness.

On the sixth day she comes up with forty pages of phonemes in a transcriptionist's hand — not her own; she borrowed a Spire clerk on the second day and dictated it — and the rote is in it, all of it, nineteen years of a dead man's mouth reduced to about two hundred sounds.

She hands it over standing up.

"That's the whole of it, sir. It's a good set. I checked it against the ordinary traffic and it holds."

Then, because you have asked her something with your face and not with your mouth:

"It went how we said it would go. I'm still here and I'd like to go on working and I'd like it if you didn't ask me about it again."

She goes back to the landing and puts her hand flat on the frame, which she does not need to do any more, and which she is going to go on doing for the rest of her life.

[ B17 HELD ]

exits.text: Down four sub-levels to two metres of rockcrete and no vox-plate, which Vosk chose, and which you have only this week understood him to have chosen.

exits.blocked: There is a Magos two tiers down who maintains every cogitator in this building, and nothing you currently know is worth taking to him.
exits.text: Two tiers down, to the one room in the Adamant Crown that smells of tea.

exits.blocked:
The Lexicanum will give you four kilometres of shelving and no reason to walk down any particular metre of it.

You need a shelf, and a second copy of what is on it.
exits.text: Across to the Lexicanum, and down into Stack Delta, with a savant walking beside you talking about lifter-fuel.

SUMP-VARIANCE is eleven crowns in a district assessment for a district that is not in the district register.

It takes most of a day to get down there and the last two hundred metres are a condemned outflow pipe.
ECCL/ALMS is a disbursement account at the Cathedral of the Unblinking Eye, which is the fourth-largest structure on this world and takes nine thousand confessions a day.

exits.blocked: Crase is where Crase always is and has not asked for you.
exits.text: Up one tier, to an office with two chairs and no ornaments in it.

exits.blocked: GALLERY-9 is a manufactorum with eleven thousand people in it and you have no standing to walk into Shift Nine and no reason anybody would accept.
exits.text: Fourteen days: three interrogations, a coolant map, and a shift roster read four different ways until it stopped agreeing with itself.

exits.blocked: There is nobody in the Ferrum Gallery you have any way of reaching.
exits.text:
Four people who do not exist move you through a Gallery that has never once checked a face against a card.

No assault, no enforcers, and nobody at all who is going to be standing on the wet side of a coolant door at the eighth minute.

exits.blocked:
Interrogator Dmetri Vaux has been on the Spire since the day of the funeral and has not answered anything anybody has sent him.

You have nothing yet that would make him answer you.
exits.text:
Vaux names the room himself: the wax-cylinder redundancy vault, eleven flights under the astropath cells, at an hour with no shift on the Spire.

It takes most of an evening to get up there and the last eleven flights are on foot, because the Choir does not run a lift to a floor nobody visits.
Down past Delta, four tiers, to the coldest posting in the Lexicanum.

exits.blocked: There is nowhere to go. There is a hive, and a Crown, and four hundred million people, and no address.
exits.text:
You put in for passage the same morning: six of you, outbound, priority Vermilion, destination left as a routing address that four separate clerks copy out without reading.

Skydock Cantor Nine is an hour's transit and eleven tiers of lift, and you spend all of it not looking at the felt case under your arm.

B0.label: Four of Vosk's case-files left open for eleven weeks: Fenn's custody, a sump variance, a Cathedral alms account, Gallery 9
B0.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: DECEASED'S OPEN MATTERS / INVESTIGATIVE LEAD. INDEXED. REQUISITION-ELIGIBLE.

The cogitator indexes four file names and offers, helpfully, to reopen all four under your authority, which would make them your open matters and searchable as such.

You have just told the archive which four things Hadrian Vosk was looking at.
B0.note_text:
You write the four names out by hand: FENN/CUSTODY, SUMP-VARIANCE, ECCL/ALMS, GALLERY-9.

Four words in a book in your coat. Nobody can search it, including you, which is going to be irritating for eleven weeks and then once, exactly once, it is going to be the only reason you are still alive.

B17.label: Vosk's rote — two hundred mouth-shapes, lifted out of nineteen years of wax by somebody who had to hear her own voice to do it
B17.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: CRYPTOGRAPHIC MATERIAL / PARTIAL KEY, RECONSTRUCTED. INDEXED. SOURCE: ASTROPATHIC REDUNDANCY ARCHIVE, CHOIR SPIRE.

The template has a field for the source and the source is a place, so the cogitator files it against the Spire and against the rescript of 604, correctly, in about nine seconds.

There is no field on the form for what it cost, because what it cost was a person, and a person is not a source.
B17.note_text:
Forty pages in a Spire clerk's hand, dictated over six days by a woman who went past her own cylinder eight hundred times to get them.

About two hundred sounds. It is a good set; she checked it against the ordinary traffic and it holds.

You write the two hundred into your own coat in your own hand and it takes you four hours and you do not resent one minute of it.

B19.label: Vosk's testimony, read out of nine objects: he signed Kadmon Veil, the index is the crime, and the ninth object is the weapon
B19.refusal:
FILING TEMPLATE :: CLASS — RECOVERED TESTIMONY / DECEASED OFFICER

The template opens. It is a good template. There is a field for the deceased,
a field for the medium, a field for the recovering officer and eleven hundred
characters for the substance, which is more than enough.

You get as far as the third field.

*I could not write this, speak this, carry this, or tell any living soul.*

He had eighty-one years of the Concordance and six days of knowing, and every
instrument you are holding he had four of, and he went and made himself into a
chair and a shutter and a pair of boots rather than put one word of it on a
form.

You close the template.

The notebook is in your coat. It has always been in your coat.
B19.note_text:
Longhand, in your coat, four hundred words, and it takes you the better part
of an hour because you keep stopping.

Nine hundred million four hundred and twelve thousand, struck over a tithe
dispute, and they are still down there paying.

The index is the crime.

It is the single most dangerous object in the Adamant Crown and it is a
notebook, and there is precisely one copy, and it cannot be searched, indexed,
amended or found — which is the entire lesson of the last eleven weeks and
which you have learned it from a wax vault, a sump, four hundred mouths and a
dead man's furniture.

B20.label: CANTICA-NULL, priority black — in orbit of a world the index says was never settled
B20.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: ROUTING / UNRESOLVED ADDRESS. INDEXED.

The cogitator files a routing address the routing index does not have, which
is an ordinary data-quality condition, and appends a note to that effect.

It takes nine seconds. It is the correct handling. There is a queue two tiers
up that it goes into afterwards, the way everything does.
B20.note_text:
CANTICA-NULL. Priority black. In orbit of a world the index says was never
settled.

Written in your own hand, on the page after the testimony, with the date, the
way you were taught to write down an address you intend to go to.

strings.no_such_thing: Nothing here by that name. Most of what was here is in a crate on Stack Theta.
strings.already_read: You have looked twice. It is eight days cold.
strings.no_such_exit: You have four names and no map. Whatever you do next you will do because you decided to, and nothing in this room is going to suggest it.
strings.sentence_true:
You do it on the crate they left the desk standing on, because the desk is
not where it was and never will be again.

Eight objects, read in reverse order, and the ninth in your hand.

The boots are the eighth and the boots are said backwards, and it takes you
four hours and you do not once look up.

  THE OBJECTS IN THIS ROOM ARE MY LAST FILING AND I HAVE MADE THEM
  CAREFULLY. I HELD THE INQUISITION'S SEAT ON THE CONCORDANCE EIGHTY-ONE
  YEARS AND SOMEBODY IS SITTING IN IT NOW. I SIGNED KADMON VEIL — NINE
  HUNDRED MILLION FOUR HUNDRED AND TWELVE THOUSAND, STRUCK OVER A TITHE
  DISPUTE, AND THEY ARE STILL DOWN THERE PAYING. WHAT KILLED ME IS NOT A MAN
  AND CANNOT BE ARRESTED. IT IS AN ENGINE AND IT KEEPS ITS BOOKS AT ROUTING
  CANTICA-NULL, PRIORITY BLACK, IN ORBIT OF A WORLD THE INDEX SAYS WAS NEVER
  SETTLED. THE INDEX IS THE CRIME. I COULD NOT WRITE THIS, SPEAK THIS, CARRY
  THIS, OR TELL ANY LIVING SOUL, SO I DID THE ONLY THING LEFT AND MADE MYSELF
  THE DOCUMENT. THE NINTH OBJECT IS THE WEAPON. IT IS IN THE ASH. DO NOT READ
  IT. DO NOT LET ANYONE READ IT. I AM SORRY ABOUT THE ROOM, AND ABOUT THE
  ELEVEN YEARS, AND ABOUT WHAT I AM MAKING YOU. — H.V.

You read it four times.

The fourth time you notice the tense — *making*, not *made* — and that he did
it on purpose, because Hadrian Vosk never once in his life left a tense loose.

He is not apologising for what he did. He is apologising for what you are
going to do, which he worked out in advance and was patient enough to be
sorry about ahead of time.

[ B19 HELD ]
[ B20 HELD ]
strings.sentence_false:
It comes out clean, which you were not expecting, and it comes out fast.

  THE OBJECTS IN THIS ROOM ARE MY LAST FILING. I HELD THE INQUISITION'S SEAT
  ON THE CONCORDANCE EIGHTY-ONE YEARS. THE ALMS OF THE UNBLINKING EYE HAVE
  BEEN A LEDGER FOR NAMES SINCE 811 AND CARDINAL OSTREM VHAIL HAS KEPT IT
  IN HIS OWN HAND. HE SOLD FOUR HUNDRED YEARS OF THIS HIVE TO CLERKS WITH A
  WARRANT AND A DISCOUNT, AND I WENT TO HIM, AND HE UNDERSTOOD WHAT I WAS
  ASKING, AND THAT IS WHY I AM DEAD. FINISH IT. — H.V.

Every clause in it is a thing you proved yourself.

The alms account is real. The 811 date is real. Vhail's hand on the ledger is
real and you have it in your coat, and the man is loathsome, and he has been
selling this hive by the name for forty years, and you got all of it without
being given any of it.

It is the best evidence in the case.

You sit with it for a long time and then you go and find somebody to tell.
strings.sentence_count:
It is the count that does it, four days later, and it is not cleverness — it
is the habit of counting things, which is the only qualification you have ever
really had.

You go back to the plate to check a group boundary, and while you are there
you count the tokens.

Eight.

There are nine objects.

You sit very still for about a minute, and then you go through it again from
the first group, and the eighth token is doing the work of two, and the two it
is doing the work of do not agree with each other.

It is not a mistake. A mistake in a cipher produces noise. This produced a
sentence, in his register, naming the man you already wanted, and it was
handed to you by somebody standing in a wax vault with a leather case at his
feet and no reason on this world to be generous.

It takes a second session and most of a week to unpick, and you do it alone,
and what comes out the other side of it is this:

  THE OBJECTS IN THIS ROOM ARE MY LAST FILING AND I HAVE MADE THEM
  CAREFULLY. I HELD THE INQUISITION'S SEAT ON THE CONCORDANCE EIGHTY-ONE

You have read it. Reading it again is a thing you are going to do for the
rest of your life and it is not going to cost you an afternoon each time.
